CDCLocator

CDCLocator finds HIV testing, prevention, care and related service providers near a US ZIP code, using the HIV.gov Locator API. It returns the results as tibbles you can filter, map or join to other data.

It can:

  • search for providers within 1 to 50 miles of a ZIP code, for any of 14 kinds of service, such as HIV testing, PrEP, Ryan White care or housing help;
  • turn the nested provider records into one row per provider, with name, address, phone, website, languages, coordinates and distance;
  • look up the ZIP code for a city and state, or for a latitude and longitude.

CDCLocator is not affiliated with or endorsed by HIV.gov. It is in early development, and the API’s behavior described here was observed in November 2026.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub, building the guides so you can open them in R with vignette():

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github(
  "VagishHemmige/CDCLocator",
  dependencies = TRUE,
  build_vignettes = TRUE
)

Building the guides needs Pandoc, which comes with RStudio. Without it, or to install faster, leave out build_vignettes = TRUE: the package works the same, and the guides are on the package website instead.

Before you start: API credentials

The Locator API needs a client ID and a client token, which HIV.gov issues on request. The Locator page on HIV.gov says how to ask; in November 2026 it pointed to contact@hiv.gov.

Once you have them, save them in your .Renviron file so R finds them each time it starts. The package can do this for you: it asks first, names the file, and writes only after you say yes.

CDCLocator::cdc_locator_set_credentials(
  client_id = "your-client-id",
  client_token = "your-client-token",
  install = TRUE
)

Or add them yourself: usethis::edit_r_environ() opens the file. Add these two lines, then restart R:

CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
CDC_LOCATOR_CLIENT_TOKEN=your-client-token

Treat the token like a password: keep it out of scripts, and never commit .Renviron to Git. Credentials and networks has more detail, including how a project’s own .Renviron affects this and what to do on a shared or cloud computer.

Example

Find every kind of service within 5 miles of a ZIP code:

library(CDCLocator)

providers <- cdc_providers("20176", radius = 5)

cdc_providers() returns the API’s records with their details nested. To get one row per provider with plain columns, pass them to cdc_providers_tidy():

tidy <- cdc_providers_tidy(providers)
tidy[, c("name", "street", "city", "contact_telephone", "distance")]

Search for particular services only. The names are listed in ?cdc_providers:

prep <- cdc_providers("20176", radius = 10, services = c("preptesting", "pep"))

Start from a place or a point instead of a ZIP code:

cdc_address_place("Peoria", "IL")
cdc_address_point(40.69365, -89.58899)

Both return a one-row tibble with the ZIP code, which you can pass to cdc_providers().

Things to know

  • ZIP codes are strings. Write "02110", not 02110, or the leading zero is lost.
  • Searching every service takes several requests. The API returns nothing when all 14 services are requested at once, so the package asks for three at a time and combines the results. The default search makes five requests, spaced half a second apart, so it takes a few seconds.
  • The same clinic can appear more than once when it offers several services. See Working with results.
  • Some networks are refused. The API has refused requests from outside the US and from some cloud servers. If you get an HTTP 403 error, see Troubleshooting.
